title: Fake sites and fake apps
hook: You search for your wallet app. The first result says "Official wallet download" and has a small "Sponsored" label. Tap it?
card1: Scammers pay for ads and copy real websites and apps. The fake looks right, but it steals what you type, or asks you to "connect" and approve something.
analogy1: A fake site is like a fake shop with the real shop's sign. Everything looks the same until you pay at the counter.
card2: When a site asks you to connect your [[wallet]] and approve a request, read it. An approval can let the site move your coins later, even after you leave.

walk.title: How a fake wallet app steals coins
walk.f1: You search for "wallet app" and tap the top ad.
walk.f2: It opens a copy of the real site with a big download button.
walk.f3: The app looks real and asks you to "restore" your wallet with your [[seed-phrase]].
walk.f4: The words go straight to the scammer, who empties the wallet.

card3: Install apps only from your phone's official store, and check the developer name and reviews. Type important website addresses yourself, or use a bookmark you saved.

search.prompt: You want to install a wallet app. Your search shows a sponsored result "WaIIet - Official" (with two capital i's), and the normal result below it.

ad.label: Tap the sponsored result and install
ad.before: You will install the app from the ad.
ad.what: The app asked you to restore your wallet with your seed phrase. Within minutes, all your practice coins were gone.
ad.why: Anyone can buy an ad, and the name used capital i's instead of l's.
ad.how: Look-alike letters, like I and l or 0 and O, make fake names look real.
ad.realLife: Don't install wallets from ads. Go to the official store and check the developer.

check.label: Open the ad, but look at the web address first
check.before: You will check the address bar before doing anything.
check.what: The address was "wallet-official-app.co". It looked odd, so you left. Nothing lost.
check.why: Checking the address is good, but fake addresses can look very convincing.
check.how: Scammers register names that sound official, with small changes.
check.realLife: Safer still: never start from an ad.

store.label: Open your phone's app store, search there and check the developer
store.before: You will search in the official store instead.
store.what: You found the real app, with millions of downloads and the right developer. Your coins are safe.
store.why: Official stores check apps, and the developer name and reviews help you spot fakes.
store.how: Fakes sometimes get into stores too, which is why the developer name matters.
store.realLife: If unsure, get the link from the wallet's own official website.

q1.prompt: A search ad says "Official wallet download". What is true?
q1.a: Ads at the top are always official
q1.b: Anyone can buy an ad, so go to the official store yourself
q1.c: If the site has a lock icon, it's safe
q1.explanation: Scammers buy ads too. Start from the official store or a bookmark you saved.

q2.prompt: A site asks you to connect your wallet and approve a request. What should you know?
q2.a: An approval can let the site move your coins later
q2.b: It's just like logging in, nothing more
q2.c: Approvals end when you close the site
q2.explanation: Read every request. Approvals can give a site permission to move your coins, and many stay until you remove them.

q3.prompt: A wallet app asks for your seed phrase right after you install it. What do you do?
q3.a: Type it in, the app needs it
q3.b: Type in only half of it
q3.c: Stop and check that the app is genuine first
q3.explanation: Only type your seed phrase when you are sure the app is genuine and you are restoring your own wallet.

misc.adOfficial: "Ads at the top are official." Anyone can buy an ad, including scammers.
misc.lockSafe: "A lock icon means it's safe." The lock only means the connection is encrypted. Fake sites have it too.
misc.connectHarmless: "Connecting is just logging in." Approvals can give a site permission to move your coins.
misc.approvalOnce: "Approvals end when I close the site." Many stay until you remove them.
misc.restoreNeeded: "The app needs my seed phrase to work." A new wallet makes its own. Only type yours in an app you are sure is genuine.
misc.halfPhrase: "Half the phrase is safe to type." Half makes the rest much easier to guess.

t1: Don't install apps or open wallet sites from ads.
t2: Read every request before you approve it in your [[wallet]].
t3: Use the official store, check the developer and type addresses yourself.
talk1: How do we check that an app is the real one before we install it?
talk2: Which important websites should we save as bookmarks?
